key_insight: Element-specific spectroscopy reveals ultrafast hole transfer from Re to Se and electron localization associated with inferred flat conduction bands in Re₆Se₈Cl₂ superatomic crystals.
engineering_relevance: Understanding site-specific charge transfer and phonon coupling could guide tuning of superatomic crystals for optoelectronic applications.
method: Probe photoexcited carriers with transient XUV spectroscopy.
Simultaneously measure the Re O₂ and Se M₄,₅ absorption edges.
Correlate spectral features to separate electron, hole, band-gap, and phonon dynamics.
evidence_signal: Correlated Re- and Se-edge measurements indicate hot-hole transfer and reveal phonon oscillations attributed to hole-mediated displacive excitation.
watch_item: Flat conduction bands are inferred from spectroscopy, and the abstract reports no device-level performance validation.
paper_title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
